title: Lack of Deprecation Backsliding Prevention
pattern: Successfully migrating old call sites of a deprecated API but failing to add static analysis blocks or linters to reject new calls to the deprecated symbol.
why_bad: Developers writing new code will copy-paste legacy examples from other areas of the codebase, continuously introducing new dependencies on the obsolete code. The migration becomes an endless, expensive game of "whack-a-mole" [337, 733].
detection: A deprecated symbol/API that is not registered in a linter rule, build-gate blacklist, or visibility whitelist.
counterexample: None. Failing to guard against backsliding of deprecated features is an operational failure.
fix: Configure lint rules or build visibility whitelists that trigger compile-time errors if any new calls to the deprecated API are introduced [337, 733, 734, 735].
source: Software Engineering at Google, Chapter 15, "Cleanup - Preventing backsliding" [337, 733, 734, 735]
